claims.text: Đơn Hàng's README process: copy template.md to a new numbered file with status Đề xuất; open a pull request holding only that ADR, whose description gives the comment deadline (usually five working days) and names the people the decision affects.
Every comment is answered in the pull request; comments that change the decision are written into the ADR's 'Ý kiến đã nhận' section, objections included.
claims.source_hint: docs/adr/README.md @ stage-3 lines 35-36; docs/adr/template.md 'Ý kiến đã nhận'

claims.text: When the comment period ends the team lead decides; the aim is to hear every objection before deciding, not for everyone to agree.
Before merging the status becomes Đã chấp nhận or Bị từ chối; a rejected ADR is still merged and kept so the same idea is not proposed again without new reasons.
Some teams call a written proposal an RFC and keep it in a separate file; Đơn Hàng keeps no separate file, the ADR at status Đề xuất plays both roles.
Recording a decision-changing comment in the ADR keeps the reason for the change with the decision rather than only in the pull request thread; an objection nobody asked for cannot be weighed.

template.md's header holds the decider (one person, by role) and the comment deadline. ADR 0008 header: status Đã chấp nhận; decider: the team lead; comment deadline: end of Friday in the first week of Sprint 17.

ADR 0008 concerns the old notifications and payments tables left in donhang, debts N1 and N2 in tech-debt-register.md, which no application code reads or writes; the register gives both 'Trả ngay' (repay now).
claims.source_hint: docs/adr/0008 @ stage-3 lines 10-15; docs/team/tech-debt-register.md @ stage-3 rows N1, N2

claims.text: ADR 0008 decision: dump both tables with pg_dump -Fc --table; a migration drops notifications first, with the same PR removing it from PostgresFixture's TRUNCATE; payments is dropped after accounting confirms reconciliation with donhang_payments.

donhang_payments is the Payments service's own database; existing payments were copied into it. Accounting objected to dropping payments at once: they check old payments at quarter end and had not checked that copy; so payments is dropped only after they confirm.
claims.source_hint: docs/adr/0008 @ stage-3 lines 46-49; STAGE.md line 15; docs/design/refund-design.md lines 89-91

claims.text: A tester asked whether integration tests rely on the tables; none reads them, but PostgresFixture empties both between tests with TRUNCATE, so each dropping migration edits that command in the same PR (added to steps 2 and 3).
ADR 0008 consequence: because the tables are not dropped together, for a while only the old payments table remains; at tag stage-3 both tables still exist and the steps run in the next sprint.
Waiting for full agreement lets any single objection hold a decision back with no end date.
A rejection is a decision too; deleting a rejected ADR loses the reasons and invites the same discussion again.
People a decision affects can know costs its author does not, so a comment period is not a formality even when a senior engineer favours the proposal.
